Sam / team — I’ve reviewed Markus’s proposed sequence and attached a focused set of redline notes. Two points I want to call out that will affect the timeline if Aurora requires changes: 

1) Data processing scope: the DPA must reflect the specific processing activities (PHI flow limitations, subprocessor notifications). If Aurora asks for additional contractual security guarantees beyond our standard exhibit, we may need a short legal call and an extra 3–5 business days.

2) Liability & indemnity: Aurora’s earlier draft requested a carve-out for security incidents that would materially increase risk. We’re willing to discuss a narrow carve but will need procurement to confirm insurance/limit thresholds — that’s often what causes a re-cycle.

Recommended schedule from Legal perspective:
- Redline exchange (MSA) — Redwood posts revised redline: 2026-06-01 (Markus).
- Aurora consolidated comments — 2026-06-04 (allows 3 business days for internal review).
- Short legal sync to triage high-risk items — 2026-06-05 or 06 (30 min).
- DPA finalization window — 2026-06-09.
- Order Form clean copy for procurement — 2026-06-11.

I’ve attached: Aurora_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf (with callouts) and a plain-language memo that maps the redlines to likely procurement questions.

If procurement needs evidence beyond SOC2 (e.g., pen-test summary, ISO attestations), flag now — we can share an executive pack but it will add 1–2 business days.

Thanks,
